editionContext.baseText: Ganjoor online transcription of Ferdowsi’s Shahnameh: the great war of Kay Khosrow with Afrasiab, sections 1 to 47.
editionContext.criticalPrintEdition: Not independently established for this online transcription.
editionContext.scope: The great war of Kay Khosrow with Afrasiab as the poem tells it, with its praise of Sultan Mahmud, through the death of Afrasiab, the death of Kavus and Kay Khosrow’s renunciation and disappearance, to the enthronement of Lohrasp; the scenes are drawn from groups of sections, not verse by verse.

Ganjoor, Ferdowsi’s Shahnameh: the table of contents

entities.label: The Shahnameh
entities.summary: The literary work in which the great war of Kay Khosrow is told.

entities.label: Ferdowsi
entities.summary: The poet of the Shahnameh.

entities.label: The great war of Kay Khosrow
entities.summary: The story of Kay Khosrow’s last war on Afrasiab to avenge Siavash – from the elephant throne to Gang-dezh, Chin, Makran and the lake of Chichast where Afrasiab is taken – and of the king’s renunciation of the throne and disappearance.

entities.label: Kay Khosrow
entities.summary: The king of Iran, son of Siavash, who fights Afrasiab to the end to avenge his father, and after sixty years of rule gives up the throne and vanishes.

entities.label: Afrasiab
entities.summary: The king of Turan, who flees from Gang-dezh to Chin and Makran and at last hides in a cave and in the lake of Chichast, where he is taken and killed.

entities.label: Shideh
entities.summary: A son of Afrasiab, who brings his father’s offer of peace and fights Kay Khosrow alone.

entities.label: Jahn
entities.summary: A son of Afrasiab, who leads thirty thousand men and later carries his father’s message from Gang-dezh.

entities.label: Garsivaz
entities.summary: The brother of Afrasiab, taken captive and put to death with him.

entities.label: Kay Kavus
entities.summary: The old king, grandfather of Kay Khosrow, to whom he writes of his victories; they pray together at Azargoshasb, and Kavus dies after Afrasiab’s death.

entities.label: The Faghfur of Chin
entities.summary: The emperor of Chin, who allies himself with Afrasiab and afterwards asks Kay Khosrow’s pardon.

entities.label: The king of Makran
entities.summary: The king who refuses Kay Khosrow passage and is defeated and killed.

entities.label: Hom
entities.summary: A pious hermit of the line of Fereydun, who hears Afrasiab lamenting in his cave, binds him and, when he escapes into the lake, finds him again.

entities.label: Rostam
entities.summary: The champion, whose counsel the king follows in the war, and to whom he gives Nimruz at the end.

entities.label: Zal
entities.summary: The father of Rostam, who reproaches Kay Khosrow for withdrawing from the world, then begs his pardon.

entities.label: Gudarz
entities.summary: The old champion, to whom the king gives his treasures; he mourns the champions lost in the snow.

entities.label: Lohrasp
entities.summary: The man Kay Khosrow chooses as his successor, to the surprise of the Iranians.

entities.label: Sorush
entities.summary: The messenger of God who tells Kay Khosrow in a dream that he may leave the world.

entities.label: Tus
entities.summary: A champion, given Khorasan and the banner of Kaveh, who follows the king to the mountain and dies in the snow.

entities.label: Giv
entities.summary: A champion, given Qom and Isfahan, who follows the king to the mountain and dies in the snow.

entities.label: Bizhan
entities.summary: The son of Giv, who brings Lohrasp before the king and dies in the snow.

entities.label: Fariborz
entities.summary: A son of Kay Kavus, who follows the king to the mountain and dies in the snow.

entities.label: Gostaham
entities.summary: A champion who follows the king to the mountain.

entities.label: Iran
entities.summary: The kingdom of Kay Khosrow.

entities.label: Turan
entities.summary: The kingdom of Afrasiab.

entities.label: The Jayhun
entities.summary: The river between Iran and Turan, which Afrasiab’s army crosses by boat and over which he flees by night.

entities.label: Gang-dezh
entities.summary: The stronghold of Afrasiab, which Kay Khosrow takes.

entities.label: Chin
entities.summary: The land of the Faghfur.

entities.label: Makran
entities.summary: The land whose king refuses Kay Khosrow passage.

entities.label: The lake of Chichast
entities.summary: The water into which Afrasiab escapes from Hom, and where he is caught again.

entities.label: Azargoshasb
entities.summary: The fire temple where Kay Khosrow and Kavus pray.

events.label: In praise of Sultan Mahmud
events.summary: The poet opens the story with a long praise of Sultan Mahmud, a lion in battle.

events.label: The elephant throne
events.summary: Kay Khosrow sits on a turquoise throne on an elephant’s back, sounds the call, gathers his great men and arrays his army against Afrasiab.

events.label: Afrasiab’s mourning and muster
events.summary: Hearing of the defeat and death of his kinsmen, Afrasiab mourns, swears revenge and sends his army over the Jayhun by boat.

events.label: The offer of peace
events.summary: The armies face each other across a trench. Afrasiab sends his son Shideh with an offer of peace; Kay Khosrow answers that Siavash was killed without guilt and will have revenge, and proposes single combat.

events.label: Kay Khosrow and Shideh
events.summary: Away from the armies Kay Khosrow fights Shideh alone and kills him; the Turks wait in vain for him to return, and Afrasiab mourns.

events.label: Afrasiab flees over the Jayhun
events.summary: Jahn brings thirty thousand men; Qaren prevails, the king prays, and Afrasiab flees by night over the Jayhun towards Gang. Kay Khosrow writes to Kavus of three battles.

events.label: The wind at Golzarriun
events.summary: The kings meet in battle; at Kay Khosrow’s prayer a strong wind rises and Afrasiab flees to Gang and writes to the Faghfur of Chin.

events.label: The message from Gang-dezh
events.summary: Kay Khosrow surrounds Gang-dezh. Jahn brings his father’s message of regret for Siavash’s blood and offer of peace; the king rejects it and swears to fight to the end.

events.label: Gang-dezh taken
events.summary: The stronghold falls; Afrasiab escapes in secret, the women of Turan lament and Kay Khosrow spares them.

events.label: Afrasiab and the Faghfur
events.summary: The Faghfur of Chin allies himself with Afrasiab. Afrasiab offers single combat; on Rostam’s advice the king declines and lays an ambush, the night attack fails, the Faghfur asks pardon, and Afrasiab crosses the water of Zereh back to Gang-dezh.

events.label: The king of Makran
events.summary: After letters to Kavus and the submission of the Khaqan and the Faghfur, the king of Makran refuses passage; Kay Khosrow defeats and buries him, crosses the sea and weeps at the walls Siavash built.

events.label: The return to Kavus
events.summary: Afrasiab flees again by night; Kay Khosrow mourns Siavash and returns to Iran, meets Kavus and the two kings pray at the fire temple of Azargoshasb.

events.label: Hom and the cave
events.summary: Afrasiab hides in a cave near Barda; the hermit Hom hears him lament, binds his arms and leads him away, but in pity loosens the bonds and Afrasiab escapes into the water.

events.label: The lake of Chichast
events.summary: Afrasiab hides in the lake of Chichast; hearing Garsivaz lament, he comes out and Hom takes him again.

events.label: The death of Afrasiab
events.summary: Kay Khosrow puts Afrasiab and Garsivaz to death with the sword; he gives thanks at Azargoshasb and spreads justice and gifts over the world.

events.label: The death of Kavus
events.summary: Kavus, at peace, prays and dies; Kay Khosrow buries him.

events.label: The king withdraws
events.summary: After sixty years of rule, with the world at his feet, Kay Khosrow fears that pride will cost him the divine glory; he closes his court and prays for weeks, and Sorush tells him in a dream that he may leave the world.

events.label: Zal’s reproach
events.summary: Zal and Rostam come to the withdrawn king. Zal says a demon has turned him from God’s path; Kay Khosrow answers with his lineage and his vengeance and his fear of hell, and Zal asks his pardon.

events.label: The king’s gifts
events.summary: Kay Khosrow gives away his treasures and lands: his treasures to Gudarz, Nimruz to Rostam, Qom and Isfahan to Giv, Khorasan and the banner of Kaveh to Tus.

events.label: The crown to Lohrasp
events.summary: To the dismay of the Iranians the king has Bizhan bring Lohrasp and gives him the crown; then he takes leave and goes to the mountain with his champions.

events.label: The king vanishes
events.summary: At a spring in the mountains the king bids his companions farewell; when the sun rises he has vanished from their sight.

events.label: The champions in the snow
events.summary: A snowstorm buries the champions who would not turn back – Tus, Giv, Bizhan and Fariborz – and Gudarz mourns; Rostam and Zal come back from the mountain.

events.label: Lohrasp enthroned
events.summary: Lohrasp sits on the throne; Zal and Gudarz pledge him allegiance and he is crowned at Mehregan.
